title: Tiered KV grooming and circuit-tempered fallback orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a resilient, observable mechanism that preserves customer-facing SLOs when downstream KV-backed stores (Redis/managed caches) degrade or become congested. The feature, "Tiered KV Grooming and Circuit-Tempered Fallback Orchestrator" (TKG-CTFO), combines lightweight pre-grooming of hot prefixes, a time-windowed circuit that is tempered by token-bucket admission, and progressive connection-pool thinning to maintain latency SLOs across multi-region topologies.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Under synthetic KV saturation (95th percentile latency > 500ms), the orchestrator engages a staged fallback within 200ms and maintains 99th percentile tail latency for API reads below 300ms for 95% of tenants during the test window.
2) Metrics are emitted for every decision: grooming hit/miss, circuit state transitions (closed->probation->open->half-open), token-bucket drop rate, and connection-pool thinning level. Dashboards and alert rules are in place.
3) Canary rollout: deploy to 3% of production tenants with automatic rollback on SLO regressions detected by the observability playbook.
4) Automated unit and integration tests covering mode transitions, back-pressure scenarios, and regional failover.
5) Runbook and incident checklist created and reviewed by SRE and Product.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- We prefer a short-lived grooming pass (50-200ms window) over eager prefetching to limit additional load on the KV store. Grooming targets top-k prefixes per tenant using recent access histograms.
- Circuits are not binary; they use a tempered approach: once error/latency thresholds cross, the circuit moves to 'probation' where a token-bucket gate allows a controlled fraction of requests to reach the KV store. This reduces thundering herd risk while preserving sample reads for warming caches.
- Connection-pool thinning reduces maximum concurrent connections per tenant/region in phases (10% steps). We avoid immediate hard limits to prevent latency cliffs.
- Multi-region failover defaults to local-first, then regional-hedging to secondary replicas when local SLOs breach for >150ms. Full cross-region failover only after sustained degradation (configurable window). This balances latency and correctness for stateful KV semantics.
- We accept additional complexity in orchestration to avoid system-wide degradations that harm high-priority tenants. The orchestrator is opt-in per deployment tier (hosted vs dedicated) with conservative defaults for enterprise customers.
implementation_notes:
- Core components: grooming scheduler (per-tenant, lightweight), tempered-circuit controller, adaptive-conn-pool manager, and a decision-telemetry emitter.
- Data flow: request -> admission filter -> grooming check (local cache hit) -> if miss then token-bucket check -> if allowed, route to KV; otherwise served degraded response path (fallback cache, stale read, or structured error depending on tenant policy).
- Telemetry: add new tags to existing span schema (circuit_state, groom_hit, admission_outcome) and expose counters/histograms for token-bucket operations.
- Backwards compatibility: provide config flags to disable grooming or token-bucket for experiments.
- Failure modes: if orchestrator itself is overloaded, default to safe-thin behavior (small fixed connection budget) and emit high-severity alerts.
testing_plan:
1) Microbenchmarks simulating 1000 tenants with realistic prefix skews to validate grooming cost.
2) Chaos test: inject 10-30% packet loss and injected latency into Redis replicas in a single region while running production-like traffic. Validate SLO preservation and rollback logic.
3) Multi-region failover rehearsal in staging with synthetic leader election and region blackouts.
4) Load tests driving token-bucket saturation to verify controlled shedding rates and downstream budget recovery intervals.
5) Smoke tests for telemetry and dashboard accuracy.
observability_and_slos:
- Primary SLOs impacted: read-99p-latency < 200ms (goal), read-error-rate < 0.1%.
- New Grafana dashboard: "TKG-CTFO / KV Resilience" (panels: groom_hit_rate, circuit_state_counts, token_drop_rate, per-tenant conn_pool_level, regional_failover_events).
- Alerts: P1 if circuit_open_fraction across tenants > 5% for > 5m; P0 if canary tenants SLO regression >10% relative to baseline.
- Perf regression guardrails integrated into CI with PR gating.
rollout_and_migration:
- Phase 0: Internal staging validation and perf tuning.
- Phase 1: Canary rollout to 3% of production tenants (low-impact orgs) for 72 hours with automatic rollback on SLO regression.
- Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% with SRE monitoring and runbook drills.
- Phase 3: Full rollout and turn-on of regional hedging for dedicated customers.
- Migration: tenants can opt-out; enterprise customers get longer probation windows.
runbook_and_incident_playbook:
- Onboarding alerts: run 'tkgctfo diagnose' script to collect recent grooming histograms, circuit transitions, and token-bucket state.
- Recovery steps: 1) Pause grooming and increase token-bucket capacity temporarily; 2) Scale KV read replicas if autoscaling is available; 3) Trigger controlled client-side soft-reads (serve cached/stale) for affected tenant groups; 4) If orchestrator misbehavior suspected, flip to safe-thin-mode and roll back.
- Post-incident: update heatmap of prefix churn and tune grooming window/thresholds.
security_and_compliance_notes:
- No new persistent customer data is stored by the orchestrator; grooming metadata is ephemeral and TTL'd.
- Telemetry includes tenant identifiers; ensure PII redaction before exporting to external systems.
- Security review required for telemetry export and config toggle controls in the Console.
notes_for_reviewers:
- Key questions: 1) Is the token-bucket rate control granularity per-tenant sufficient, or do we need per-route buckets? 2) Are the grooming selection heuristics (top-k prefixes) fair across noisy tenants?
- Please review the Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/TKG-CTFO+Design (internal).
- Proto PR with controller and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234
- Observability PR (dashboard + alerts): https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/567
